lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The merchant-payment result is duplicated under the hospital practicum, where it does not fit.
items.because: The practicum concerns a hospital network, while the same 2,300-merchant onboarding result appears under Harbor Payments.

items.says: Experience is not listed newest-first.
items.because: Crestline ends in 2023, while the Harbor Payments internship ends in 2024, making the chronology harder to scan.

items.says: Education appears before Experience.
items.because: The relevant work and product transition appear after the degrees, so readers encounter them later than necessary.

items.says: The bullet claims fewer late deliveries when it only shows a lower reported rate after changing the calculation.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments can lower the rate without changing delivery performance.

items.says: The bullet uses a first-person possessive.
items.because: “My” makes it read like a sentence and draws attention away from the redesign.

items.says: The bullet credits the full pick-error reduction to the redesign without establishing causation.
items.because: Other changes or changes in error recording could also explain the reduction.

items.says: The bullet credits the forecast-error reduction to consensus forecasting without establishing causation.
items.because: Demand patterns, data, or other process changes could also affect forecast error.

items.says: The bullet does not establish that the rollout saved 1,800 net driver hours annually.
items.because: It is unclear whether the figure was measured or projected, and gross or modeled reductions may not equal net annual savings.

items.says: “Led the rollout of” is less direct than “Rolled out.”
items.because: It delays the action without adding information.

items.says: The bullet attributes the conversion increase to the flow change without establishing causation.
items.because: A before-and-after result cannot separate the flow’s effect from seasonality, other changes, or random variation.

items.says: The 35% conversion change lacks context for interpreting its size.
items.because: It is unclear whether it means relative or percentage-point growth, and no comparison period or baseline is given.

items.says: The annual chargeback-loss result is buried after the methods.
items.because: A scanning reader must reach the end of the bullet to find it.

items.says: The closing phrase repeats the roadmap connection.
items.because: It does not add a new result.

items.says: The opt-in comparison does not establish that the redesign caused the onboarding outcome.
items.because: Merchants who chose the new flow may differ from those who stayed on the old one.

items.says: The measurement bullet gives the comparison setup but no result.
items.because: A scanning reader must connect it to the next bullet to understand the outcome.

items.says: The 9-to-4-day result is presented as caused by the redesign without an adequate comparison.
items.because: The opt-in groups may differ in ways that also affect onboarding.

items.says: The bullet does not say what product or launch work the product lead owned.
items.because: It shows the app’s reach and food-rescue result but not the individual contribution.

items.says: “That would have been thrown away” repeats the implication of “surplus-food.”
items.because: It lengthens the bullet without clarifying the achievement.

items.says: The bullet treats interviews as proof that students missed pickup windows.
items.because: Without independent corroboration, interviews establish what participants reported, not verified behavior or how common it was.

items.says: “Each week” and “a week” repeat the same cadence.
items.because: The staffing reduction remains clear with only one weekly phrase.

items.says: The sessions bullet does not say what the practicum changed or produced.
items.because: Readers can see who met and what they discussed but cannot assess what the work accomplished.

items.says: The intake change and staff adoption do not show what improved for patients or staff.
items.because: Adoption does not show whether intake became faster, errors fell, or another outcome improved.
